implementation_notes: On Node the address is the AMQP property: amqplib declares an exclusive server-named callback queue, publishes with replyTo and correlationId, and the service answers with channel.sendToQueue(msg.properties.replyTo, ...) copying the correlation id. RabbitMQ's direct reply-to (replyTo: 'amq.rabbitmq.reply-to') removes the per-request queue at the cost of consuming before publishing. Prefer these over an invented application header: every AMQP client language reads the same property.
idiom_name: AMQP replyTo property (amqplib) on an exclusive callback queue
pitfalls: The exclusive callback queue dies with the connection, so a reconnect loses the address while workers may still answer to the old name.
The correlation check must precede resolving: with one callback queue per client a late or duplicated reply otherwise settles the wrong promise.
Blocking the Node event loop inside a consumer callback delays every channel on that connection and makes reply timeouts fire spuriously.
